scientific_question: At fixed initially assigned native larvae, does randomized adequate access to edible host foliage change the effect of introduced Sericinus presence on adult production in native Atrophaneura?
source: Hashimoto and Ohgushi 2023, Ecol Evol 10.1002/ece3.10164; Takagi and Miyashita 2008 DOI 10.1603/0013-8746(2008)101[392:HPQIDI]2.0.CO;2
design: 2x2 competitor present/absent x food-supply support/natural, whole independent plant/enclosure randomization in complete treatment-balanced source blocks
endpoint: flight-capable native adults per initially assigned native neonates
estimand: equal-weight mean over blocks of (clamp+competitor − clamp alone) − (natural+competitor − natural alone), with cage-level proportions as response
mechanistic_problem: Final food-remaining ratings are post-outcome and may increase because early native butterfly death stops feeding. Clamp can alter tissue quality and handling, not just biomass.

data_contract.allocation: existing randomized plant_id, block_id, treatment, competitor_present, food_clamp CSV with all four arms per block
data_contract.fates: plant_id,larva_id,species,fate; one row per initially assigned native larva, including deaths and censoring
data_contract.resource: plant_id,observation_datetime,native_larvae_alive_n,native_late_instar_alive_n,accessible_leaf_area_cm2,fresh_leaf_area_added_cm2,present_leaf_age_class,added_leaf_age_class; time-offset ISO timestamps, native_late is living 3rd–5th instars, source leaf class young/mature/mixed/none/unknown

fates.unknown_bounds: Lower possible lifetime flight-capable adults = observed flight-capable adults / original larvae; upper includes original assigned larvae still alive in pupal diapause, other alive nonemerged pupae and truly unobserved followup. Diapause is NOT a confirmed failure or observed adult.
fates.previous_unsafe_code_rejected: pupa_no_adult is ambiguous because it may be a living diapausing pupa; software rejects it in favor of confirmed death or pending live pupa

quality_gates: Treatment allocation hash and independent plant/cage IDs match across inputs
No animal outcome is used to define eligibility or treatment
Every originally assigned native larva has a fate record
All four treatments present and balanced within each predeclared block
Resource visits equal to prespecified expected_n_resource_visits within each cage
Missing resource accessibility remains unknown, never converted to zero
Clamp achieved a real and reportable food access contrast under competitor presence; do not subset to plants where the clamp worked
Report floor breach and observed supplementation by randomized arm; clamp quality confounding requires separate controls
At least 3 truly independent source blocks before any block-bootstrap interval; otherwise report point contrast only
Do not infer food quantity's unique mediated causal effect from a total supplementation intervention
At scheduled resource visits, independently count native living larvae and living 3rd–5th instar larvae; late <= alive <= initially assigned, and no sorting by whether late-stage survivors remain.

Report per-treatment number of living 3rd–5th-instar observations, missing leaf area among these, and proportion below prospectively established access floor; a zero-late-survivor cage is not evidence that food was sufficient.
Report fresh added leaf age class independently of accessible leaf quantity; a significant food-supplementation effect may be driven by leaf quality or handling.
Predefine seasonal photoperiod, temperature, census duration, diapause diagnostic and overwinter followup in each block; guard against differential observation horizons across arms.
Never mark a live diapausing pupa as dead or as a permanently unsuccessful adult; report alive pupae in each arm and use partial-identification bounds for ultimate adult viability.
A treatment effect on early adult eclosion may represent shifted emergence timing rather than reduced survival; examine adult timing and diapause separately.
bootstrap: 2,000 bootstrap resamples of whole source blocks with replacement, fixed seed 20261010, 95% percentile CI; this is a procedural plan, not power-guaranteeing significance
randomization: Use pre-existing randomized assignment, do not reassign after observing larvae
sensitivity: Lower/upper ITT outcome bounds from censoring and a fully documented primary complete-fates contrast; cannot drop attrition post-hoc

interpretation.positive: Supplying accessible edible foliage weakens competitor harm. Compatible with temporary shortage but tissue chemistry or handling remains possible.
interpretation.null: No supported moderation; interpret only if the clamp created a real between-arm supply contrast and independent replication sufficed.
interpretation.negative: Supplying foliage worsens competition difference; cannot call protective food access without quality controls.
interpretation.unidentified: If clamp never changes access or there are inadequate independent replicate plants, no claim about transient shortage.

paper_boundary: Causal mechanism in an invaded butterfly system feeding on native Aristolochia, NOT the separate chocho human-redistributed host-plant GEB paper

source_stage_specific_consumption.article: Hashimoto & Ohgushi 2023, Ecology and Evolution, Table 1, DOI 10.1002/ece3.10164
source_stage_specific_consumption.units: mg leaf dry mass consumed per larva over indicated stage interval, original experimental reference not a minimum leaf standing crop threshold
source_stage_specific_consumption.implication: Predefine food-access monitoring in BOTH early and 3rd–5th instars; most cumulative consumption occurs late. Source mass cannot simply be converted to minimum accessible fresh leaf area without independent calibration.

revised_reason: The previous concise resource ledger lacked living instar data, so stage-specific resource shortages could not be checked despite 3rd–5th instar demand dominating cumulative feeding.
endpoint_interpretation: Primary experimental effect remains assigned food-access strategy × assigned competitor exposure; late-instar accessibility is a post-treatment manipulation diagnostic, NOT a conditioning variable for the primary ITT effect.

life_history_prior_art.paper: Takagi & Miyashita (2008), Host Plant Quality Influences Diapause Induction of Byasa alcinous, DOI 10.1603/0013-8746(2008)101[392:HPQIDI]2.0.CO;2
life_history_prior_art.taxonomic_identity: Byasa alcinous is a recognized taxonomic synonym/combination of Atrophaneura alcinous (NCBI Taxonomy 85299).
life_history_prior_art.key_difference: 2008 used A. kaempferi from a Chiba mountain population, not A. debilis from Kyoto cages; cannot assume magnitude/generalizability.
life_history_prior_art.experimental_conditions: 20°C, 16:8 L:D photoperiod, 3 independent source mothers; randomized larvae to soft vs tough A. kaempferi leaves; duration, early survival, and diapause scored.
life_history_prior_art.published_results: Hard leaves reduce early survival and prolong larvae; almost every pupated larva from tough leaves entered diapause (all but one); not a new effect.
life_history_prior_art.measurement_boundary: Diapausing pupa alive is NOT a confirmed immature death, nor a failure to ever produce an adult. A fixed 30d adult window detects early emergence but cannot infer lifetime adult output unless overwintering and later emergence monitored.

primary_estimand_adjudication: Predefine a standardized adult follow-up horizon before trial. Count flight-capable adults by that date separately from known live diapausing and other nonemerged pupae; report lower and upper eventual adult-capable proportion bounds, and categorical diapause probability per original cohort. Overwinter and recheck pupae using predefined conditions to resolve eventual adult success. Unknown fate or living pupa remains unresolved, not known mortality.
